blocks.html: Games preservation refers to the ongoing efforts to archive, preserve, and maintain access to video games and other forms of interactive media, ensuring their cultural and historical significance is recognized and protected. As games evolve and older platforms become obsolete, preserving these works becomes increasingly important in order to understand the development of the medium. Games preservation is essential for the study of the history, design, and cultural significance of games, as well as for the appreciation and continued enjoyment of these works by future generations.

Games preservation involves a wide range of activities, including the collection and storage of physical media, the preservation of digital files, and the maintenance of hardware and software necessary for playing older games. It also encompasses the documentation and archiving of development materials, marketing materials, and game-related ephemera that provide valuable context for the study of the medium. The preservation of games can be seen as an act of reverence, acknowledging the importance of games as cultural artifacts and ensuring that their unique experiences and stories remain accessible for future players, scholars, and enthusiasts. As the field of game and play studies continues to grow, games preservation will play an increasingly vital role in sustaining the rich heritage of the medium and deepening our understanding of its history and impact.
